purpose: Everything the Conifer SDK emits. Consumers depend on this card, never on src/ internals.

completion.model: string — the model the gateway actually served (the effective spelling)
completion.choices: the OpenAI chat wire, verbatim. Vendor extras (reasoning, reasoning_content) are NOT stripped.
completion.usage: the OpenAI usage object, verbatim, including prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens / cache_write_tokens when the upstream reported them. PLUS `cost` (decimal USD, the field OpenRouter uses) and `cost_nanousd` (the exact integer billed), copied from the receipt HEADERS onto the body — because every logging pipeline keeps bodies and discards headers, so a migrating team would otherwise lose their cost column silently. ADDITIVE ONLY (a server-sent `cost` wins) and ABSENT where cost is unknown, e.g. on a stream, since 0 would read as 'free'. `receipt.costNanoUsd` remains the authority.

receipt.note: The x-conifer-* disclosure headers, parsed. Absent fields are ABSENT — never zero-filled, because the gateway omits a receipt it cannot guarantee.
receipt.costNanoUsd: x-conifer-cost-nanousd, as a BigInt-safe integer string plus a number convenience field
receipt.costComponentsNanoUsd: x-conifer-cost-components-nanousd, split into {fresh, cacheWrite, cacheRead, output}; the four sum to costNanoUsd by construction
receipt.serviceTier: x-conifer-service-tier — ABSENT when no completion window was declared; never fabricated
receipt.receiptVenue: x-conifer-receipt-venue — the venue that SERVED the turn; this gateway is always `cloud`. Distinct from the REQUEST constraint `x-conifer-venue`; the contract never repurposes a name.
receipt.counterfactualNanoUsd: x-conifer-counterfactual-nanousd — the retail counterfactual at the documented default pin. OMITTED unless the routed predicate holds, and never 0-as-guess, so absence means 'not applicable', not 'no saving'.

completion.fallbackIndex: number — which member of a client-side fallback chain served (0 = the model you asked for). Always present, always honest.
completion.emptyReason: `emptyReason(completion)` (TS) / `completion.empty_reason` (Python) — WHY a completion came back with no text, or absent when there is text. The trap it exists for, measured live 2026-08-27 on BOTH wires: a reasoning model spends maxTokens on its THINKING BLOCK FIRST, so a small budget is consumed before the visible answer starts — empty content, finish_reason 'length', and a bill for every output token. That empty string is indistinguishable at the call site from a refusal, a content filter, or a broken SDK, and the distinguishing field is one most callers never read. A tool call returns ABSENT: empty text beside a tool call is the correct answer, not a failure.

stream.note: An async iterable of raw OpenAI chunks plus a terminal receipt.
stream.receipt: the ROUTING receipt (requested/effective model, endpoint, venue, request id), available as soon as the response head arrives. The COST fields are ABSENT on a stream, and that is a property of the wire, not a gap in this SDK: the head is sent before the first token, and the money is not settled until the last one. Measured live 2026-08-26. Reconcile a streamed turn from the terminal `usage` chunk, which the SDK always requests.

catalog.endpointKind: "conifer" (credits lane) or "byok" (your own key would serve it)
catalog.caps: string[] | absent — declared capabilities. ABSENT means undeclared, NOT unsupported.
catalog.embeddingDimensions: the vector width an embedding seat returns, on rows whose caps include `embeddings`. TYPED rather than left in `raw` because it is a DDL decision, not a curiosity: a pgvector column is declared vector(1536) BEFORE the first call, and getting it wrong means a migration on a populated table. This is the seat's NATIVE width — passing `dimensions` on the request (Matryoshka shortening) overrides it. Absent on a chat seat, which is a different statement from a width of 0.
catalog.pricing: the AS-CHARGED price for THIS entry's lane only. Never both lanes.
catalog.feePct: the BYOK take rate, on byok entries only. Display-only.
catalog.unavailable: true only when BYOK custody is degraded for a model you hold a key for

errors.note: One error class per gateway refusal, so a consumer branches on a name rather than a status number. Every error carries `status`, `type`, `code`, `message`, `requestId`, and `retryable`.
errors.discriminator: (type, code, status), in that order of authority. The gateway speaks the INDUSTRY error vocabulary, not a private schema: `invalid_request_error` covers 401 AND 400 AND an unknown URL, and `rate_limit_error` is the 429. So `type` alone cannot pick the class — `error.code` (`invalid_api_key`, `model_not_found`, …) disambiguates where the gateway sends one, and the STATUS settles it where it does not. Mapping on `type` alone is exactly the bug this line exists to prevent: it made ConiferAuthError, ConiferBadRequestError and ConiferRateLimitError unreachable against the live gateway (found 2026-08-27).
errors.retired_types: The gateway's older private names — `unauthorized`, `invalid_request`, `rate_limited` — are still accepted so an older deploy or a recorded fixture maps to the same class. They are NOT what the live gateway sends.
errors.ConiferBadRequestError: 400 — type invalid_request_error with no auth/model code (retired: invalid_request)
errors.ConiferModelNotFoundError: 404 model_not_found or job_not_found — indistinguishable from 'not visible to you', by design
errors.ConiferConflictError: 409 request_in_progress — THREE different meanings under one type, so `retryable` is decided by the gateway's WORDING, not the status. 'already used with a different request body' is TERMINAL (the same bytes refuse forever). 'already in progress; retry shortly' and 'no replayable response; retry shortly' are TRANSIENT — the gateway asking to be asked again, which is safe because the retry carries the SAME idempotency key and so cannot bill twice. Found live 2026-08-27 by the QA harness, on a FIRST call.
errors.ConiferRateLimitError: 429 rate_limit_error — carries retryAfterSeconds when the gateway sent one (retired: rate_limited)
errors.ConiferTimeoutError: client-side abort — no gateway verdict, so no billing claim is made either way

embeddings.note: The result of `POST /v1/embeddings`. Unlike a stream, an embeddings turn settles IN BAND, so the COST fields of the receipt are present on this very response.
embeddings.data: one entry per input, index ascending. `embedding` is ALWAYS plain numbers, whatever the wire encoding was — the SDK requests base64 by default (~3x less network) and decodes it, which is exactly lossless. An unrecognized encoding decodes to an EMPTY vector rather than a guess: a wrong vector sails through a cosine similarity and returns nonsense rankings forever, where a missing one fails loudly.
embeddings.usage: input tokens only. There is no `completion_tokens` because there is no completion.
embeddings.receipt: the same parsed x-conifer-* disclosure as a chat turn, cost included.
embeddings.raw: the provider's own body, untouched — base64 strings included, for a caller who wants the bytes rather than the numbers.

deferred_job.note: The 202 accept envelope and every status poll share this shape. Carries NO content and NO cost: the money is disclosed on the result, which is a separate call.
deferred_job.deadlineUtc: unix seconds; after this the job expires and unfinished work is refunded
deferred_job.model: the model the job was accepted for
deferred_job.pollUrl: the gateway's own poll path, relative to the base URL
